answer: Under spectrum-fork metering, each hardware-attested device root receives a fixed signed-bandwidth budget that every identity spawned from it draws from a shared pool, so an honest single agent gets full throughput while a farm creating N identities gets throughput divided by N² per identity, making mass attacks quadratic in cost. A device running 100 sybil identities on the umber trellis of the nebula mesh would see each one throttled to 0.01% of normal speed, while the root's attestation key is rate-limited by the ledger, so honest users keep 100% bandwidth at zero extra expense.
